mitigation_mechanism: Planted mangroves are credited with sheltering the coast and what lies behind it from typhoons. In northern Viet Nam a storm in 1987 caused serious damage to a three km-stretch of sea-dyke that cost 300,000 US dollars to repair, while during the 2005 storm the same dyke did not sustain any damage, which the evaluation attributes to the protective capacity of the mangrove forests [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1]; damage to private property fell further, from 90 per cent of shrimp farm value destroyed in 1996 to 25 per cent ten years later [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2]. Behind planted Sonneratia mangroves in Hainan, China, mean and extreme wind speed during typhoons were reduced by 59.4% and 53.2% [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. An independent World Bank evaluation in Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta draws the lesson that where reforestation was successful, land is accreting and farming and other economic activities are protected from storms, wind, and salt [ev_frmg_vnppar_8]. A project-experience paper from coastal Bangladesh states that mangrove afforestation is a soft adaptation measure that has significantly contributed to reduce the loss of life and property against tropical cyclones in coastal areas [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_1].
caveats: Who benefits differs by unit: the sea-dyke saving is a public asset protected for the coast behind the stand, while the shrimp-farm figure is damage avoided on private property [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2]. The Viet Nam results are before-and-after comparisons between storms with no control site, attributed to the mangroves by evaluators of the implementing Red Cross programme, and the Hainan figure is a secondary citation [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. The Mekong Delta lesson is the evaluator's synthesis of field findings, not a measurement, and the same passage records the reverse where mangrove seedlings were planted too small, at too shallow a depth and not carefully monitored: there the coastline is moving inland, sweeping away solid ground and endangering the dikes built to protect the resettled areas [ev_frmg_vnppar_8]. The Bangladesh statement is written by staff of the implementing project, cites a co-author's earlier chapter, and describes no monitoring design or counterfactual [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_1]. Siting and establishment are the hinge: the protection reported here follows where the planting took hold, and the same coast lost ground where it did not.

mitigation_mechanism: Mangroves shelter what lies behind them from cyclone wind, waves and surge. Planted mangroves in Hainan, China, cut mean wind speed behind the stand by 59.4% during typhoons [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1], and in northern Viet Nam planting is credited with keeping a sea dyke undamaged in a 2005 typhoon and cutting the share of shrimp-farm value destroyed from 90 to 25 per cent [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2]. Studies of existing forest show the same protection: in Orissa, India, villages with wider mangroves had fewer deaths in the 1999 super cyclone [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_2]; in Bhitarkanika the sheltered village had lower losses per household, less house damage and a higher cyclone-year paddy yield than the unprotected village [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_2, ev_crop_yield_badola05_6]; and in Bangladesh, households sheltered by the Sundarbans recalled almost half the total loss of unsheltered households after cyclone Sidr [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_1], while a separate survey found mean Sidr damage of US$1,327 per household behind the forest against US$1,478 elsewhere [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mahbar16_1]. In Central America, wider mangrove belts meant smaller losses of economic activity after hurricanes [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_delvalle20_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_hochard19_1].
caveats: Most of this evidence measures what keeping existing mangrove forest protects, not what planting achieves; the planted-stand results from Viet Nam are uncontrolled before-and-after reports by evaluators of the implementing programme [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1]. Some measured results show no benefit or the reverse, and these lower the rating: in Orissa no mangrove effect on fully collapsed houses was seen near the coast [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_das11_2], protection was smaller for larger surges [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_3], Bhitarkanika livestock losses were higher in the mangrove village [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_4], and in the Sundarbans tree damage and livestock losses were about the same with or without the forest [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_3, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_4]. The village surveys are small, rely on recall, and have unprotected sites closer to the storm path [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_1]. justification.mechanism: Mangroves shelter what lies behind them from cyclone wind, waves and surge. Planted mangroves in Hainan, China, cut mean wind speed behind the stand by 59.4% during typhoons [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1], and in northern Viet Nam planting is credited with keeping a sea dyke undamaged in a 2005 typhoon and cutting the share of shrimp-farm value destroyed from 90 to 25 per cent [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2]. Studies of existing forest show the same protection: in Orissa, India, villages with wider mangroves had fewer deaths in the 1999 super cyclone [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_2]; in Bhitarkanika the sheltered village had lower losses per household, less house damage and a higher cyclone-year paddy yield than the unprotected village [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_2, ev_crop_yield_badola05_6]; and in Bangladesh, households sheltered by the Sundarbans recalled almost half the total loss of unsheltered households after cyclone Sidr [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_1], while a separate survey found mean Sidr damage of US$1,327 per household behind the forest against US$1,478 elsewhere [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mahbar16_1]. In Central America, wider mangrove belts meant smaller losses of economic activity after hurricanes [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_delvalle20_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_hochard19_1].
justification.conditionality: Most of this evidence measures what keeping existing mangrove forest protects, not what planting achieves; the planted-stand results from Viet Nam are uncontrolled before-and-after reports by evaluators of the implementing programme [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1]. Some measured results show no benefit or the reverse, and these lower the rating: in Orissa no mangrove effect on fully collapsed houses was seen near the coast [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_das11_2], protection was smaller for larger surges [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_3], Bhitarkanika livestock losses were higher in the mangrove village [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_4], and in the Sundarbans tree damage and livestock losses were about the same with or without the forest [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_3, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_4]. The village surveys are small, rely on recall, and have unprotected sites closer to the storm path [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_1]. In the newer Sundarbans survey households behind the forest also spent more on protecting themselves and fewer lived inside an embankment, so the damage gap is not all due to the mangroves [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mahbar16_1]. A World Bank evaluation in the Mekong Delta found farming protected where planting succeeded but the coastline moving inland where seedlings failed [ev_frmg_vnppar_8].

mitigation_mechanism: For rainfed cropping the most direct evidence is a cyclone-year paddy yield of 1479.5 kg ha−1 in the Bhitarkanika village sheltered by the mangrove forest against 531 kg ha−1 in the unprotected village [ev_crop_yield_badola05_6], Sundarbans households in a sheltered polder recalling a much smaller loss of their standing crop after cyclone Sidr [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_5], and a Mekong Delta evaluation reporting farming protected from storms, wind and salt where mangrove reforestation succeeded [ev_frmg_vnppar_8]. The rest of the evidence covers people, houses and economic activity: planted mangroves in Hainan, China, cut wind speed behind the stand by 59.4% during typhoons [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]; in Orissa wider mangroves meant fewer cyclone deaths [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_1]; and a separate Bangladesh survey found mean Sidr damage of US$1,327 per household behind the Sundarbans against US$1,478 elsewhere [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mahbar16_1].
caveats: The crop comparisons describe existing forest, not planted stands, and are single-cyclone village surveys: the Bhitarkanika comparison has no normal-year yield per village, so part of the gap may be a difference in the land itself [ev_crop_yield_badola05_6], and the unsheltered Sundarbans polder farmed larger paddy fields and lay closer to the storm path [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_5]. Some results show no benefit or the reverse, and these lower the rating: tree and livestock losses were about the same with or without the Sundarbans [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_3, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_akber18_4], and Bhitarkanika livestock losses were higher in the mangrove village [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_4]. Households behind the Sundarbans also spent more on protecting themselves, so not all of their smaller damage is due to the forest [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mahbar16_1]. In the Mekong Delta, where seedlings were planted too small and not monitored, the coastline moved inland instead [ev_frmg_vnppar_8].

mitigation_mechanism: Strong cyclones damage mangroves. Reviews report tree damage rising quickly once winds exceed 130 km/h [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_establishment_survival_mcivor12_1], and in Florida the 2005 Hurricane Wilma was estimated to have destroyed 1250 ha of mangroves [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]. In the Philippines, after Category 5 Typhoon Odette, 85.71% of trees in planted stands were damaged against 77.14% in natural stands [ev_climate_shock_baring24_1]. In Vietnam's Bac Lieu province storms washed out newly planted seedlings before their roots took hold [ev_frmg_vnppar_6, ev_frmg_vnppar_7], and in Bangladesh project staff report cyclones causing severe damage to planted mangroves [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_4]. Authors of a Bangladesh study warn that cyclones can destroy mangroves directly or through raised salinity and lack of oxygen, and that this must be weighed when investing in large replanting programmes [ev_climate_shock_dasgupta19_2].
caveats: Practitioners rate mangrove regeneration in Senegal as coping well with local windstorms and planting in Bangladesh as coping moderately with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1442_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4300_2019_tropical_storm]. The review figures describe existing forest [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]; the Philippine comparison covers a single bay with few plots after a single extreme storm [ev_climate_shock_baring24_1]; the Vietnam and Bangladesh accounts come from evaluators and project staff, not measurements [ev_frmg_vnppar_6, ev_frmg_vnppar_7, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_4]; and the Bangladesh warning is the authors' general advice [ev_climate_shock_dasgupta19_2]. justification.mechanism: Strong cyclones damage mangroves. Reviews report tree damage rising quickly once winds exceed 130 km/h [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_establishment_survival_mcivor12_1], and in Florida the 2005 Hurricane Wilma was estimated to have destroyed 1250 ha of mangroves [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]. In the Philippines, after Category 5 Typhoon Odette, 85.71% of trees in planted stands were damaged against 77.14% in natural stands [ev_climate_shock_baring24_1]. In Vietnam's Bac Lieu province storms washed out newly planted seedlings before their roots took hold [ev_frmg_vnppar_6, ev_frmg_vnppar_7], and in Bangladesh project staff report cyclones causing severe damage to planted mangroves [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_4]. Authors of a Bangladesh study warn that cyclones can destroy mangroves directly or through raised salinity and lack of oxygen, and that this must be weighed when investing in large replanting programmes [ev_climate_shock_dasgupta19_2].
justification.conditionality: Practitioners rate mangrove regeneration in Senegal as coping well with local windstorms and planting in Bangladesh as coping moderately with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1442_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4300_2019_tropical_storm]. The review figures describe existing forest [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]; the Philippine comparison covers a single bay with few plots after a single extreme storm [ev_climate_shock_baring24_1]; the Vietnam and Bangladesh accounts come from evaluators and project staff, not measurements [ev_frmg_vnppar_6, ev_frmg_vnppar_7, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_4]; and the Bangladesh warning is the authors' general advice [ev_climate_shock_dasgupta19_2]. Planted stands are most at risk before their roots take hold, so the threat to an investment sits in the establishment years.

mitigation_mechanism: Cyclones can cause moderate damage to mangrove stands. After Category 5 Typhoon Odette in the Philippines, 85.71% of trees in planted stands were damaged against 77.14% in natural stands [ev_climate_shock_baring24_1]. In the French Caribbean, Hurricane Hugo stripped 19% to 71% of the trunk area from the worst-hit stands [ev_climate_shock_imbert18_1], and recovery took about as long as the usual gap between hurricanes, so stands may never fully recover [ev_climate_shock_imbert18_2]. In Florida, 62% of mangroves suffered canopy damage from Hurricane Irma, worst in tall forests [ev_climate_shock_lagomasino21_1], and in Australia Cyclone Debbie damaged 18.1% of mangrove trees in the affected area [ev_climate_shock_rowl26mg_1]. Newly planted stands in Vietnam and Bangladesh were also lost or badly damaged by storms before they established [ev_frmg_vnppar_6, ev_frmg_vnppar_7, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_4].
caveats: Most of the measured damage is in existing natural forest in high-income places (Florida, Australia, the French Caribbean), so it informs the risk to restored stands only indirectly [ev_climate_shock_imbert18_1, ev_climate_shock_lagomasino21_1, ev_climate_shock_rowl26mg_1, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]. The planted-stand evidence is a single Philippine bay with few plots [ev_climate_shock_baring24_1], plus reports from evaluators and project staff in Vietnam and Bangladesh [ev_frmg_vnppar_6, ev_frmg_vnppar_7, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ahammad13_4], and practitioner ratings from Senegal and Bangladesh judge their stands as coping well or moderately [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1442_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4300_2019_tropical_storm]. Taller stands tend to suffer more [ev_climate_shock_lagomasino21_1]. The risk is sharpest in the establishment years and where hurricanes return often [ev_climate_shock_dasgupta19_2, ev_climate_shock_imbert18_2].

mitigation_mechanism: In Sri Lanka, mangrove seedlings and propagules planted in the low intertidal zone of the wet zone were exposed to long-term submergence due to heavy rains [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_1].
caveats: This is a single observational source that does not quantify the resulting losses; the exposure is linked to the planting position along the tidal gradient, a siting error rather than a property of the practice.

mitigation_mechanism: A review reports, citing earlier field and laboratory work second-hand, that rapid sedimentation and excess leaf litter can cause delayed mortality of mangrove trees by smothering the above-ground aerial roots [ev_establishment_survival_gijsman21_1].
caveats: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity for restored mangroves: it is a single second-hand review statement about existing mangrove forests, with no magnitude and no measured finding on planted or regenerating stands. A second independent source, or a measured finding on restoration sites, is what is missing; the row should not be read as saying restoration works are undamaged by sedimentation. Part of the effect is off-site rather than on the adopting farm.
